personality_one_liner: A high-utility, lightning-fast mobility interface combining map-first architecture with premium iOS-native spacing and stark contrast.

spacing.rule: Use iOS-native rhythmic spacing. Maintain a minimum of 'md' margin between cards and safe screen edges. Floating map actions should have 'lg' inset from the screen edges to allow map context to bleed through.

do's: Floating Action Buttons (FABs) over the map.
Top sticky header (if any) to let the map bleed underneath.
Bottom sheet drag handles and background layer if it acts as a floating map overlay.
dont's: Form inputs, standard list rows, or primary bottom CTA (keep CTA solid).

screens.name: Customer - Auth
screens.purpose: Mobile number entry and OTP verification for quick customer onboarding.

states.error: Inline text below OTP input with shake animation.

screens.layout: Minimalist top-aligned typography. Single column input. 'Send OTP' button fixed to bottom using KeyboardAvoidingView with safe-area padding.

screens.name: Customer - Home & Ride Booking
screens.purpose: Full-bleed map showing current location and a bottom sheet to enter destinations and select service type.

states.loading: Skeleton loader for the vehicle selector cards.
states.error: Toast overlay if location services are disabled.

screens.layout: Map in the background (flex: 1). Floating drawer/menu button top left (glassmorphism). Bottom Sheet containing 'Where to?' input. Once expanded, shows 2-col vehicle grid (ZipBike, ZipDelivery) and fare estimates. Sticky solid 'Confirm Ride' CTA at the bottom of the sheet.

screens.name: Customer - Searching & Tracking
screens.purpose: Shows the radar matching state and then transitions to live driver tracking.

states.loading: Pulsing radar animation (Reanimated) emitting from user's map marker.
states.error: BottomSheet changes to 'No captains found' with a Retry button.

screens.layout: Map with route polyline. Bottom Sheet locked to 30% height displaying Captain profile (image, name, rating, vehicle number), ride OTP, and a horizontal action row for Call/Chat/SOS.

screens.name: Captain - Dashboard
screens.purpose: Map overview with online toggle and earnings summary.

states.empty: Map shows offline state (greyed out or overlay).

screens.layout: Map background. Top-center floating pill toggle for Online/Offline. Floating card at the bottom displaying today's earnings, total rides, and 'Cash in Hand'.

screens.name: Captain - Incoming Request
screens.purpose: High-priority overlay when a new ride is matched.
screens.layout: Modal or 80% BottomSheet. Large typographic focus on Fare, Pickup distance, and Drop-off location. Two large action buttons at the bottom: 'Decline' (surfaceTertiary) and 'Accept' (brandPrimary).

screens.name: Captain - Active Ride
screens.purpose: Turn-by-turn navigation overlay and ride status management.
screens.layout: Map with polyline. Top glass banner showing next turn instructions. Bottom sheet containing Customer info and a slider or large pill button to update status ('Reached', 'Start Ride', 'Complete').

map_placeholder.alt: Aerial street view for offline map fallback

instructions_to_main_agent: Ensure map components (react-native-maps) span full-screen where applicable, utilizing StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject so they sit completely behind overlays.
Implement bottom sheets using @gorhom/bottom-sheet. For customer ride flow, the sheet dynamically changes snap points based on state (Location Search -> Vehicle Selection -> Matching -> Active Ride).
Use Phosphor icons consistently across all UI buttons and indicators.
Strictly follow the color palette. Pure near-black (#111111) is used as the primary action color. Do not use generic blues or purples anywhere in the system.
For the 'Searching & Matching' animation, use react-native-reanimated to create a pulsing/scaling circular overlay on the map marker.
In the Captain Incoming Request view, ensure a countdown visual (circular progress or prominent text timer) is central to the hierarchy, driving urgency.
Apply iOS-native glassmorphism to floating map actions (e.g., hamburger menu, recenter button) so they overlay beautifully against the map.
